segments: The tenth discourse.
The Arab kings.
Baanes, the commander of the Romans,
and also the son of Shahrbaraz the Persian,
who, when his father was killed, had taken refuge with the Romans,
and also the sacellarius of the king who was in Edessa,
gathered sixty thousand horsemen.
And they met the Arabs in the region of Hims,
and the Romans were defeated,
and forty thousand of them perished,
while most of them were drowned in the Yarmuk River.
The son of Shahrbaraz,
however, having escaped alive, sent to Umar:
"Give me an army, and I will subjugate the Persians for you."
Now the daughters of Khosrow, who were among the captives held by the Arabs, informed Umar of what Shahrbaraz and his son had done to Khosrow and his sons,
and that they were treacherous:
"Do not be deceived by their words."
And when Umar accepted their words, he sent to Hims,
and impaled the son of Shahrbaraz on a stake.
And he came to Damascus and gave terms to the Damascenes,
and they opened the gates to them.
And from there he sent Khalid with an army to the region of Aleppo and Antioch,
and many people perished.
For even in the monastery of Mar Simeon of the Pillar,
when men and women, boys and girls were assembled on the feast,
the Arabs came upon them,
and took them all captive.
And at that same time, Sa'd also set out from Yathrib,
and pitched his camp near Kufa, which is 'Aqula.
And Yazdegerd also sent an army,
and they pitched their camps on the Euphrates.
And the Persians sent an Arab spy to scout the Arabs.
Now he, when he approached, saw a Ma'addite sitting to ease nature,
and chewing bread.
And the spy said to him in the Saracen tongue:
"What are you doing?" And the Ma'addite replied:
"Behold,
as you see,
I am putting out the old,
and taking in the new."
And immediately he returned and informed the Persians:
"The people I saw are stripped and bare,
yet exceedingly stout-hearted."
And he related to the general what he had heard,
and that their victory was from God.
And when they joined battle,
the Persians were defeated,
and were pursued as far as Ctesiphon on the Tigris.
One of the Persian warriors fled from a Ma'addite who was pursuing behind him,
and entered a village nearby,
and a certain peasant hid him.
He, seeing that the Ma'addite who was pursuing was bare and had only a reed in his hand,
went in {OCR?}
